why: rclcpp's wait-set protocol, and this stage is where it is answered once. An entity declares how many wait-set slots of each kind it needs, the executor assembles one `rcl_wait_set_t` out of every entity in every callback group, blocks in `rcl_wait`, then asks each ready entity to hand its data back (`take_data`) and to execute. RFC-0002 puts ONE executor on ONE RTOS task, shared by every node in that tier, and drives entities DIRECTLY through the RMW vtable -- `has_data` / `drive_io` / `next_deadline_ms` over a fixed arena indexed by `HandleId`, dispatched FIFO. No wait set is ever constructed, so there is nothing for an entity to describe itself to and no ready-set to hand back. What a user loses: blocking on an externally assembled set of entities, and extending the executor with a third-party object by implementing `Waitable`. The pubsub, service, timer and action stages decline the per-entity halves and point here.
